A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same YAQA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama and Gemma quantization experiments measuring KL divergence, perplexity and zeroshot accuracy, alongside Hessian-sketch and incoherence analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds evaluated GuidedQuant and CBQ comparisons and a quantitative cross-model KL example.

M1.justification: The two Hessian sketches and YAQA rounding procedure are retained. v1 Equation 10 matches v2 Equation 5 after accounting for LDL-factor notation, and Algorithm 1 and the iterative implementation remain unchanged. The new convergence framework analyzes this existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use RedPajama calibration and Wikitext2, C4, ARC-C, ARC-E, BoolQ, HellaSwag and PIQA evaluation coverage. The new Llama 1/2 examples introduce model configurations and analyses within existing benchmark tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds GuidedQuant to Table 1 across four Llama configurations and three bitrates, and adds a CBQ-versus-YAQA-B comparison in Table 5. These substantially extend the evaluated comparison methods. LDLQ, DiscQuant and Google QAT remain; PV-Tuning remains an indirect discussion without evaluated comparison rows.

E3.justification: New Table 5 introduces Llama 2 7B experiments with INT2, INT3 and INT4 without finetuning, while Appendix A.4 compares Llama 1/2 7B distributions. The existing calibration budgets, evaluation splits, 8192-token perplexity/KL evaluation and finetuning settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a quantitative case study showing that similar perplexities can accompany substantially different model distributions. The existing sketch sample-size sensitivity, cosine similarities, spectral analyses, incoherence trace analysis and experiment without incoherence processing are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard errors or significance tests. The retained discussion of Hessian-estimator variance does not introduce experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial GuidedQuant and CBQ results. For example, 4-bit Llama 3.2 3B zeroshot accuracy is 64.10 for GuidedQuant versus 63.31 for YAQA-B; INT2 Llama 2 7B C4 perplexity is 11.30 for CBQ versus 9.22 for YAQA-B. Appendix A.4 also adds a cross-model KL of 0.197.

T1.justification: v2 adds structural nilpotence degree, convergence Lemmas 1–2 and their proofs, plus a GuidedQuant complexity analysis. The earlier proxy-error and cosine-similarity bounds are retained and renumbered. The Hadamard normalization is corrected from 1/2 to 1/sqrt(2). New Lemma 2 states an additive SND formula, although its appendix proof uses the sum minus one.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes scalable Hessian sketches, quantizer-independent rounding and approximately 30% lower KL with theoretical guarantees. v2 makes convergence characterization, the claimed first end-to-end quantization error bounds, and provable superiority over GPTQ/LDLQ central contributions. This substantially strengthens the theoretical claims while retaining the principal empirical claim.

C2.justification: v1 conditions its tighter-bound comparison on comparable weight-error norms and sufficiently low rank; v2 omits the comparable-norm qualification and repeatedly presents YAQA as provably better. It also adds explanations based on GuidedQuant's missing output-side feedback and limitations of descent methods, while removing the qualification that recovery finetuning was optimized for LDLQ.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's repository link and retains only a future-release statement; v1 had conflicting availability statements. Reported sketch costs change from approximately 30 to 20 GPU-hours for A and from under 50 to approximately 30 for B, without establishing a matched-hardware speedup. v2 also omits the explicit 256K-sequence reference-Hessian detail for the retained cosine-similarity plots.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against full-model adaptive rounding and descent-based quantization, adding GuidedQuant, CBQ and structured matrix-multiplication work. GuidedQuant becomes a central theoretical and empirical comparison. Broader pruning and optimizer background and associated citations are removed or compressed, alongside a stronger theoretical-novelty position.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Rounding theory now precedes Hessian-sketch construction, QAT is integrated into the first-order-method comparison, and the appendices gain new sections. An ethics and reproducibility statement is added and acknowledgments are removed.

P2.justification: Document-wide retypesetting changes heading, citation and code-listing styles and substantially rearranges displays. The original plots are reused but resized and relocated, with Figures 1 and 3 exchanging numbers. QAT and finetuning tables exchange order, Table 1 expands with GuidedQuant rows, and a new CBQ table is added.

improvement.justification: The GuidedQuant and CBQ comparisons address useful comparison gaps, and the reorganized explanation and corrected Hadamard normalization are beneficial. However, the newly emphasized convergence theory contains a disagreement between Lemma 2 and its proof, while conditional bound reasoning becomes unqualified superiority claims. The new claim of winning in all metrics also conflicts with GuidedQuant's higher accuracy in several Table 1 settings. These gains and weaknesses affect different central aspects of the paper, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
